key_insight: CFD-driven symbolic regression learns compact, interpretable corrections to a RANS transition model, improving predictions while retaining only 11 of 21 candidate terms.
engineering_relevance: More reliable transition predictions can improve estimates of skin friction, heat transfer and losses in turbomachinery.
method: Correct intermittency production and destruction activation functions using pressure-gradient polynomials and bounded exponentials of local flow features.
Fit coefficients with gradient-free, solver-in-the-loop optimization accelerated by POD-Kriging field surrogates.
Select elastic-net hyperparameters through bi-level optimization with leave-one-case-out cross-validation.
evidence_signal: Trained on mean-velocity data from wall-resolved LES of ERCOFTAC T3 flat plates, the model improved LS89 turbine-cascade heat-transfer predictions without retraining at all four operating points, reducing errors by up to 70%.
watch_item: Residual transition-onset and transition-length errors indicate that flat-plate-only training limits generalization to turbine flows.
paper_title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
